summary: Both sides are a single static, spatially-uniform colour driven only by wall-clock time of day, with the same 07:00 dawn anchor and the same smooth warm-to-white ramp shape, but the port's whole colour-temperature range is shifted much whiter (mean per-channel delta 48/255, max 83) and its daylight window ends an hour early (19:00 vs 20:00).
observations: STRUCTURE (both sides): every rendered frame is ONE colour across the entire rig. Dumps at 60 px strip, 7 px strip and a 16x16 grid all report exactly 1 unique RGB triple per frame on both sides. No spatial structure exists on either side, so there is nothing to compare on the structure axis beyond 'both uniform'.

MOTION (both sides): completely static in simulated time. 240 s / 2 fps survey and 60 s / 5 fps survey both post motion avg 0, min 0, max 0, motionLit 0, zeroMotionFrames = 100% of captured frames, brightnessTrend steady, on BOTH sides. The pattern's only time axis is the harness's pinned wall clock, which does not advance. Neither side animates at all — this is a static field per JUDGE.md, so the fps/regime/autocorrelation machinery is a no-op here.
CONTROLS: meta.json reports controls: [] on BOTH sides; --probe-controls prints '(no settable controls)' for orig and port. No control-surface mismatch.

INVARIANTS (both sides): output is identical across --seed 1 vs --seed 1234, across --pixels 7 / 60 / 16x16 grid, and across dates (same time-of-day at wall-clock +0/+30/+91/+182/+273 days gives byte-identical colour on both sides). No seasonal model, no randomness, no rig dependence on either side. Value channel is pinned: meanR = 255 at every hour on both sides, so neither side ever dims — 'natural light' is expressed purely as colour temperature (saturation), never as brightness.

TIME-OF-DAY CURVE, ORIGINAL (swept 24 h at 10-min resolution, 1-min at the edges): flat night colour (255,106,12) — a deep amber, HSV hue ~23 deg, sat 0.95 — held from 20:00 through 07:00. Ramp begins at 07:01 and rises smoothly to a peak at ~13:30 of (255,218,194) — a warm peach/cream, hue ~24 deg, sat 0.24 — then descends symmetrically, reaching the night colour again at exactly 20:00. Daylight window = 07:00-20:00 (13 h), centred 13:30. Normalized saturation follows a clean parabola: norm = ((t - 13:30) / 6.5 h)^2 fits every sampled point to within a quantization count.

TIME-OF-DAY CURVE, PORT: flat night colour (255,146,39) — a lighter orange, hue ~30 deg, sat 0.85 — held from 19:00 through 07:00. Ramp begins at 07:01 (same dawn anchor as the original) and rises to a peak at 13:00 of (255,254,250) — effectively pure white, sat 0.02 — then descends symmetrically to the night colour at exactly 19:00. Daylight window = 07:00-19:00 (12 h), centred 13:00.

DIVERGENCE 1 — MIDDAY IS TOO WHITE. At the peak the original is a clearly warm peach (255,218,194, sat 0.24); the port is (255,254,250, sat 0.02), visually indistinguishable from white. Side-by-side PNGs at wall clock 13:00 make this obvious: orig renders a peach wash, port renders a blank white field. The original never desaturates past sat 0.24; the port goes essentially all the way to neutral.

DIVERGENCE 2 — NIGHT IS TOO PALE. Night/base colour: orig (255,106,12) vs port (255,146,39). The port's resting amber is 40 counts higher in green and 27 higher in blue (sat 0.85 vs 0.95) — a noticeably lighter, more yellow-orange candle colour rather than the original's deep ember orange.

DIVERGENCE 3 — DAYLIGHT WINDOW AN HOUR SHORT AT THE EVENING END. Dawn is identical (both first move at 07:01), but the original's ramp runs until 20:00 while the port clamps to night at 19:00. Minute-resolution dumps confirm: at 19:30 orig is (255,130,39), still descending; port has been flat at (255,146,39) for 30 minutes. Consequently the original's curve is centred at 13:30 and the port's at 13:00.

MAGNITUDE OF THE COLOUR GAP over the full 24 h (144-point sweep at 10-min steps): mean per-channel max |delta| = 48/255, worst = 83 at 08:40 (orig 255,168,94 vs port 255,212,177). The largest saturation gap is 0.325 at 09:00 (orig sat 0.580 vs port sat 0.255). The port is warmer-shifted-toward-white at every single hour of the day; there is no hour where the port is more saturated than the original.

RAMP SHAPE also differs beyond the endpoint rescale: normalising each side's saturation between its own night and peak values, the original follows an exact squared-distance-from-noon law, while the port's normalized curve decays faster than that near the middle of the day (e.g. at 25% of its own day elapsed the original is at 0.29 of its night-to-noon range, the port at 0.15). So re-scaling the port's endpoints alone would not fully reproduce the original's daytime progression.

The one accidental near-agreement: at 19:00 the original happens to sit at (255,148,64), close to the port's night colour (255,146,39) — a coincidence, not a match. A judge sampling only that instant would wrongly call the sides equal.
Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors: false on both), and neither errored (compileError / runtimeError null on both sides in every run).
feedback: The port's night/base colour is too pale. Original resting colour is RGB (255,106,12) (HSV hue ~23 deg, sat 0.95); the port emits (255,146,39) (hue ~30 deg, sat 0.85). Deepen the low end by ~40 counts of green and ~27 of blue.

The port's midday colour is far too white. Original noon peak is RGB (255,218,194) — sat 0.24, a visibly warm peach. The port peaks at (255,254,250) — sat 0.02, indistinguishable from white. The original's warm-white daylight never becomes neutral; clamp the top of the port's colour-temperature range so the minimum channel bottoms out near 193, not near 250.

The port's daylight window is an hour short at the evening end. Both sides begin ramping at 07:01, but the original returns to its night colour at exactly 20:00 while the port clamps at 19:00. Extend sunset from 19:00 to 20:00; the original's curve is symmetric about 13:30 with a 6.5-hour half-day, the port's about 13:00 with a 6-hour half-day.

Match the ramp LAW, not just the endpoints. The original's normalized saturation is exactly ((hoursFromNoonCentre) / 6.5)^2 — a parabola in time between its night and peak colours — checked at 10-minute resolution across the whole day. The port's normalized curve falls off faster than quadratic (at 25% of its own daylight elapsed it is at 0.15 of its range where the original is at 0.29), so simply rescaling the port's two endpoint colours will still leave a mismatch through mid-morning and mid-afternoon.

Everything else already matches and should be preserved: uniform single colour over the whole rig, fully static within a frame-time window, full brightness (R pinned at 255) at all hours with no dimming, no controls, no seed/rig/date dependence, and the 07:00 dawn anchor.

For verification of a fix: sweep --wall-clock over 24 h at 10-minute steps (base 1755993600 = 00:00 UTC, add 600*n) with --seconds 1 --dump "0" and compare pixel 0 on both sides. Target is per-channel |delta| <= 2 at every one of the 144 sample points; the current port averages 48 and peaks at 83 (08:40).
